newsitem.title: UK: Royal & Sun puts Fran cost at $20 mln. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 10/9]
newsitem.headline: Royal & Sun puts Fran cost at $20 mln. [CORRECTED 00:30 GMT 10/9]

text.p: Britain's biggest insurer, Royal & Sun Alliance, said on Monday it expected claims from hurricane Fran in the U.S. would cost the group around $20 million (corrects from 20 million stg).

"We're looking at the moment at about $20 million (corrects from 20 million stg)...We're not expecting that figure to move...It's a fairly wide mix of domestic and commercial claims," a spokeswoman told Reuters.

Hurricane Fran hit North Carolina at the end of last week killing at least 15 people and causing at least $625 million of insured damage, making Fran the most destructive hurricane in terms of insured damage in the U.S. this season.
U.S. based insurers said losses would be large, but manageable.
One Lloyds of London catastrophe underwriter said initial reports based on data from catastrophe modelling agencies suggested that insured damage from Fran would not exceed $1.0 billion.
"It doesn't look like it will be a significant number for the reinsurance market," he said, adding that brokers were not being notified of many claims.
Two other UK insurers, General Accident Plc and Guardian Royal Exchange Plc said they had limited exposure in the area hit by Fran and did not expect large bills from the hurricane.
